items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: Then there was a saxophone and violin player, Ali Laguerre. He said, well, maybe I'll make the trip. I said, well, why not the three of us get together and we go together and we stick together and we look for work over there.

ctx.x: Well, when you came back to New Orleans from Chicago, what happened then? Did you work any music jobs or anything?

You mean here in the city? Yes. No, no. I didn't. I didn't. I just came and visited with my mother, you know. And then I went back. I went back to Chicago. And when I went back to Chicago, there was a producer around there, Jerry Mills, a stage producer, putting on shows. And he had a job for me in Springfield, Illinois, in a cabaret there. And I went. There was a great. He's a great pianist now, but I can't think of his name that I met there. And he was a young fellow just starting then, you know, playing in…

if I was gonna make any money, you know. And so he told me, well, the idea was he had the telegram. He showed me the telegram from the Victor in the Columbia, telling him to bring a blues singer for audition, you know. And so he said, I would get all my transportation paid and everything, and I told him, could I get an advance? I wanted to make sure. So he said, yes, he asked me what I wanted, I told him. And so then I said, well, I'd go, and I went to New York and made a test for the Columbia and the OK, and…
